slot.brief: a piecewise function with an unknown constant at a joint; find k by equating left and right limits for continuity/differentiability

stem: If f(x) = { [sqrt(1 + 4kx) - sqrt(1 - 4kx)]/x + 1 for x < 0; 3k + 3 for x = 0; [ln(1 + 3kx)]/x + 3 for x > 0 } is continuous at x = 0, then k =
working: Left-hand limit L = lim x->0- { [sqrt(1 + 4kx) - sqrt(1 - 4kx)]/x + 1 }. Rationalizing gives ratio 8kx/[x(sqrt(1 + 4kx) + sqrt(1 - 4kx))], whose limit is 4k; hence L = 4k + 1. Right-hand limit R = lim x->0+ { ln(1 + 3kx)/x + 3 } = 3k + 3. For continuity, L = f(0) = R, so 4k + 1 = 3k + 3, giving k = 2.
solution:
For continuity at $x=0$, the one-sided limits must equal $f(0)=3k+3$.
$$\lim_{x\to0^-}f(x)=4k+1,\qquad \lim_{x\to0^+}f(x)=3k+3$$
Equating gives $4k+1=3k+3$, hence $k=2$.
